sentences.text: Aztecodus was an extinct cartilaginous fish that lived during the Devonian period. It possessed unique broad teeth with widely divergent cusps and a crenulated cutting edge.
The genus Aztecodus was described by Long and Young in 1995. It is named after the Aztec Siltstone found in southern Victoria Land, Antarctica.
The only known species is A. harmsenae, named in honor of sedimentologist Dr. Fraka Harmsen.
It is debated whether Anareodus statei is a junior synonym of Aztecodus harmsenae.
